results.title: Exponent vectors as points of the plane
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The map from exponent vectors of monomials in two variables to $\mathbb{R}^2$ sends $e = (e_0, e_1) \in \mathbb{N}^2$ to the point $(e_0, e_1) \in \mathbb{R}^2$.

results.title: Newton support
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $f$ be a polynomial in two variables $x_0, x_1$ over a commutative semiring $k$. The Newton support of $f$ is the set of exponent vectors $(e_0, e_1) \in \mathbb{N}^2$ of the monomials $x_0^{e_0} x_1^{e_1}$ with nonzero coefficient in $f$, viewed as points of $\mathbb{R}^2$.

results.title: Newton polygon
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $f$ be a polynomial in two variables over a commutative semiring $k$. The Newton polygon of $f$ is the convex hull in $\mathbb{R}^2$ of the Newton support of $f$, the set of exponent vectors of the monomials with nonzero coefficient in $f$, viewed as points of $\mathbb{R}^2$.

results.title: Interior of the Newton polygon
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a polynomial $f$ in two variables over a commutative semiring $k$, the interior of the Newton polygon of $f$ is its topological interior as a subset of $\mathbb{R}^2$.

results.title: Boundary of the Newton polygon
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a polynomial $f$ in two variables over a commutative semiring $k$, the boundary of the Newton polygon of $f$ is its topological boundary in $\mathbb{R}^2$: the closure of the Newton polygon minus its interior.

results.title: Restriction of a polynomial to a set of exponents
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $f$ be a polynomial in two variables over a commutative semiring $k$, and let $\Gamma \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$. The restriction of $f$ to $\Gamma$ is the polynomial formed by the terms of $f$ whose exponent vector, viewed as a point of $\mathbb{R}^2$, lies in $\Gamma$; the other terms are dropped.

results.title: Membership in the Newton support
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ be a polynomial in two variables over a commutative semiring $k$. A point $x \in \mathbb{R}^2$ lies in the Newton support of $f$ if and only if $x$ is the exponent vector $e \in \mathbb{N}^2$ of some monomial with nonzero coefficient in $f$, viewed as a point of $\mathbb{R}^2$.

results.title: The Newton support of the zero polynomial is empty
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every commutative semiring $k$, the Newton support of the zero polynomial in two variables over $k$ is the empty subset of $\mathbb{R}^2$.

results.title: The Newton polygon of the zero polynomial is empty
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every commutative semiring $k$, the Newton polygon of the zero polynomial in two variables over $k$ is the empty subset of $\mathbb{R}^2$.

results.title: The Newton support lies in the Newton polygon
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every polynomial $f$ in two variables over a commutative semiring $k$, the Newton support of $f$ is contained in the Newton polygon of $f$, the convex hull of the Newton support in $\mathbb{R}^2$.

results.title: The interior of the Newton polygon lies in the polygon
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every polynomial $f$ in two variables over a commutative semiring $k$, the interior of the Newton polygon of $f$ in $\mathbb{R}^2$ is contained in the Newton polygon of $f$.

results.title: Edge restriction to the empty set
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every polynomial $f$ in two variables over a commutative semiring $k$, the restriction of $f$ to the empty set, that is, the sum of the terms of $f$ whose exponent vector, viewed as a point of $\mathbb{R}^2$, lies in $\emptyset$, is the zero polynomial.

results.title: Edge restriction to the whole plane
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every polynomial $f$ in two variables over a commutative semiring $k$, the restriction of $f$ to all of $\mathbb{R}^2$, that is, the sum of the terms of $f$ whose exponent vector, viewed as a point of $\mathbb{R}^2$, lies in $\mathbb{R}^2$, is $f$ itself.

results.title: Kourovka Problem 11.97 (simple groups with a given set of character values)

The problem is due to S. P. Strunkov.

results.title: Kourovka Problem 11.97 has a negative answer

results.title: Liebeck–Pyber problem on the class number and nilpotent subgroups

results.title: The class number can exceed the order of every nilpotent subgroup
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is a finite group $G$ such that the number $k(G)$ of conjugacy classes of $G$ is greater than $|N|$ for every nilpotent subgroup $N$ of $G$.

results.title: Base relators of the Kropholler group
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $F$ be the free group on $x, y$, viewed inside the free group on $x, y, t$. The base relators are the elements $[[a, b], [c, d]]$ and $[a, b]^2$ for all $a, b, c, d \in F$.

results.title: Twist relators of the Kropholler group
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: In the free group on $x, y, t$, the twist relators are the two elements $t x t^{-1} y^{-1}$ and $t y t^{-1} (x y)^{-1}$; they encode the relations $t x t^{-1} = y$ and $t y t^{-1} = x y$, so conjugation by $t$ acts as the automorphism $\varphi \colon x \mapsto y,\ y \mapsto x y$.

results.title: The Kropholler group
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: The Kropholler group $G$ is the group with generators $x, y, t$ whose relators are the base relators, namely $[[a, b], [c, d]]$ and $[a, b]^2$ for all $a, b, c, d$ in the free group $F$ on $x, y$, together with the twist relators $t x t^{-1} y^{-1}$ and $t y t^{-1} (x y)^{-1}$.

results.title: Rational cohomological dimension 4 of the Kropholler group (Kourovka 12.41)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be the Kropholler group. This is the proposition that $H^4(G, M) \neq 0$ for some $\mathbb{Q}G$-module $M$, and $H^n(G, M) = 0$ for every $\mathbb{Q}G$-module $M$ and every integer $n > 4$; that is, the cohomological dimension of $G$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ is $4$.

results.title: The Kropholler group has rational cohomological dimension 4
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be the Kropholler group. Then $H^4(G, M) \neq 0$ for some $\mathbb{Q}G$-module $M$, and $H^n(G, M) = 0$ for every $\mathbb{Q}G$-module $M$ and every integer $n > 4$. This resolves Kourovka Notebook Problem 12.41 by P. H. Kropholler, which asks whether this cohomological dimension is 3 or 4.

results.summary: Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring with residue field $k$, and let $g \in A[X]$ be a monic polynomial whose reduction $\bar g \in k[X]$ modulo the maximal ideal of $A$ is irreducible. results.title: Finite separable residue extensions lift to finite DVR extensions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring with residue field $k$, and let $L$ be a finite separable field extension of $k$. Then there is a discrete valuation ring $B$ with an $A$-algebra structure such that $B$ is finitely generated as an $A$-module and the structure map $A \to B$ is a local homomorphism, together with an isomorphism of $k$-algebras between the residue field of $B$ (a $k$-algebra via $A \to B$) and $L$.

results.title: Spectral norm of a positive semidefinite matrix
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ be a positive semidefinite complex square matrix indexed by a nonempty finite set. Then the operator norm of $A$ with respect to the Euclidean ($\ell^2$) norm equals the largest real part of a root of the characteristic polynomial of $A$. Since these roots are real, this is its largest root.

results.title: $n$-Lagrange spectrum

results.summary: Let $L_1$ be the classical Lagrange spectrum and let $F$ (Freĭman's constant) be the infimum of the real numbers $c$ with $[c, \infty) \subseteq L_1$. Then for every integer $n \ge 1$, $[nF, \infty) \subseteq L_n \subseteq M_n$, where $L_n$ is the $n$-Lagrange spectrum and $M_n$ is the $n$-Markoff spectrum.

results.title: The $n$-Lagrange spectrum is closed
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every integer $n \ge 1$, the $n$-Lagrange spectrum $L_n$ is a closed subset of $\mathbb{R}$.

results.title: The $n$-Lagrange spectrum is the closure of its quadratic-irrational values
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n \ge 1$, let $\lambda_n$ be the $n$-Lagrange approximability, and let $P_n$ be the set of real numbers $\alpha$ such that $\alpha = \lambda_n(\xi)$ for some quadratic irrational $\xi$, that is, an irrational real number with $a\xi^2 + b\xi + c = 0$ for some integers $a \ne 0$, $b$, $c$. Then the $n$-Lagrange spectrum $L_n$ is the closure of $P_n$ in $\mathbb{R}$.

results.title: Isolated minimum of the $p$-Lagrange spectrum for primes below 2000
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every prime $p < 2000$, the $p$-Lagrange spectrum $L_p$ has a least element $\alpha$ with the following properties: $\alpha$ is an isolated point of $L_p$, that is, there is $\varepsilon > 0$ such that every $\beta \in L_p$ with $|\beta - \alpha| < \varepsilon$ equals $\alpha$; $\alpha$ is irrational; and $\alpha = \sqrt{r}$ for some rational number $r$.

results.title: The prime $67$ and continued fraction digits $1$ and $2$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For an irrational real number $\xi$, define its complete quotients by $\xi_0 = \xi$ and $\xi_{k+1} = 1/\{\xi_k\}$, where $\{\cdot\}$ denotes the fractional part, and its continued fraction digits by $a_k = \lfloor \xi_k \rfloor$. Let $p < 2000$ be a prime. Then there is no irrational $\xi$ such that the digits of both $\xi$ and $p\xi$ eventually all lie in $\{1, 2\}$ if and only if $p = 67$.

results.title: Phase of an exponent vector
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an angle vector $\theta \in \mathbb{R}^n$ and an exponent vector $e \in \mathbb{Z}^n$, the real phase of $e$ at $\theta$ is $\sum_{j} e_j \theta_j$.

results.title: Torus character
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an angle vector $\theta \in \mathbb{R}^n$, the torus character at $\theta$ sends an exponent vector $e \in \mathbb{Z}^n$ to $\exp\bigl(i \sum_{j} e_j \theta_j\bigr) \in \mathbb{C}$.

results.title: Torus character as a monoid homomorphism
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an angle vector $\theta \in \mathbb{R}^n$, the torus character $e \mapsto \exp\bigl(i \sum_{j} e_j \theta_j\bigr)$, viewed as a map from the additive group $\mathbb{Z}^n$ written multiplicatively to the multiplicative monoid of $\mathbb{C}$, is a monoid homomorphism: it sends $0$ to $1$ and sums to products.

results.title: Evaluation on the unit torus
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an angle vector $\theta \in \mathbb{R}^n$, evaluation at the point $(\exp(i\theta_1), \dots, \exp(i\theta_n))$ of the unit torus is the $\mathbb{C}$-algebra homomorphism from complex Laurent polynomials in $n$ variables to $\mathbb{C}$ that, writing $X^e$ for the monomial with exponent vector $e \in \mathbb{Z}^n$, sends $\sum_e c_e X^e$ to $\sum_e c_e \exp\bigl(i \sum_{j} e_j \theta_j\bigr)$.

results.title: Normalized box integral
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a function $f \colon \mathbb{R}^m \to \mathbb{R}$, the normalized box integral of $f$ is $(2\pi)^{-m} \int_{[0, 2\pi]^m} f(x) \, dx$, the integral taken with respect to Lebesgue measure (and equal to $0$ when $f$ is not integrable on the box).

results.title: Logarithmic Mahler measure
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a complex Laurent polynomial $F$ in $m$ variables, the logarithmic Mahler measure of $F$ is the real number $(2\pi)^{-m} \int_{[0, 2\pi]^m} \log |F(e^{i\theta_1}, \dots, e^{i\theta_m})| \, d\theta$, the integral taken with respect to Lebesgue measure.

results.title: Integer vectors of length one
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The additive isomorphism from $\mathbb{Z}^1$, the group of functions $\{0\} \to \mathbb{Z}$ under pointwise addition, to $\mathbb{Z}$ that sends a function $e$ to its value $e(0)$.

results.title: Identification of one-variable Laurent polynomials
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The $\mathbb{C}$-algebra isomorphism from complex Laurent polynomials whose exponents are vectors $e \in \mathbb{Z}^1$ (functions $\{0\} \to \mathbb{Z}$) to complex Laurent polynomials $\mathbb{C}[T, T^{-1}]$ in one variable, induced by the additive isomorphism $\mathbb{Z}^1 \cong \mathbb{Z}$, $e \mapsto e(0)$. Writing $X^{e}$ for the monomial with exponent vector $e$, it sends $c\,X^{e}$ to $c\,T^{e(0)}$.

results.title: Golden factorial exponent
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, the golden factorial exponent $\alpha(n)$ is the least positive integer $m$ with $n! \le \varphi^m$, where $\varphi$ is the golden ratio. This is the sequence OEIS A214048.

results.title: Every factorial is at most a positive power of the golden ratio
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\varphi$ be the golden ratio. For every natural number $n$ there is an integer $m \ge 1$ with $n! \le \varphi^m$.

results.title: Defining property of the golden factorial exponent
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\varphi$ be the golden ratio and, for a natural number $n$, let $\alpha(n)$ be the least positive integer $m$ with $n! \le \varphi^m$. For every natural number $n$, $\alpha(n) \ge 1$ and $n! \le \varphi^{\alpha(n)}$.

results.title: Minimality of the golden factorial exponent
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\varphi$ be the golden ratio and, for a natural number $n$, let $\alpha(n)$ be the least positive integer $m$ with $n! \le \varphi^m$. If $n$ and $m$ are natural numbers with $m \ge 1$ and $n! \le \varphi^m$, then $\alpha(n) \le m$.

results.title: Golden factorial exponent of $1$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\varphi$ be the golden ratio and, for a natural number $n$, let $\alpha(n)$ be the least positive integer $m$ with $n! \le \varphi^m$. Then $\alpha(1) = 1$.

results.title: Golden factorial exponent of $2$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\varphi$ be the golden ratio and, for a natural number $n$, let $\alpha(n)$ be the least positive integer $m$ with $n! \le \varphi^m$. Then $\alpha(2) = 2$.

results.title: Alternating-sign Fibonacci sequence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The alternating-sign Fibonacci sequence (OEIS A181716) is the integer sequence $(d_m)_{m \ge 0}$ defined by $d_0 = 0$, $d_1 = 1$ and $d_{m+2} = d_{m+1} + d_m + (-1)^{m+2}$ for every natural number $m$.

results.title: Recurrence of the alternating-sign Fibonacci sequence
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $m$, the alternating-sign Fibonacci sequence $d$ satisfies $d_{m+2} = d_{m+1} + d_m + (-1)^{m+2}$.

results.title: First values of the alternating-sign Fibonacci sequence
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The alternating-sign Fibonacci sequence $d$ satisfies $d_0 = 0$, $d_1 = 1$, $d_2 = 2$, $d_3 = 2$ and $d_4 = 5$.

results.title: Midy's theorem, general form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and $n$ a natural number such that $p$ divides $10^{2n} - 1$ but does not divide $10^n - 1$. Let $Q = (10^{2n} - 1)/p$ and write $Q = 10^n H + L$ with $0 \le L < 10^n$, so that $L$ is the number formed by the last $n$ decimal digits of $Q$ and $H$ the number formed by the remaining digits. Then $H + L = 10^n - 1$.

results.title: Browder's demiclosedness principle
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If `T` is nonexpansive, `u n ⇀ x` weakly, and `u n - T (u n) → 0`, then `T x = x`.

results.title: Fixed points of a nonexpansive map are weakly sequentially closed
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The fixed-point set of a nonexpansive map is weakly sequentially closed: if every `u n` is a fixed point of `T` and `u n ⇀ x` weakly, then `T x = x`.

results.title: Integer Laplacian of a graph
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a simple graph $G$ on a finite vertex set $V$, the integer Laplacian of $G$ is the $V \times V$ integer matrix $L$ with $L_{uu} = \deg u$ for every vertex $u$, $L_{uv} = -1$ when $u \ne v$ are adjacent, and $L_{uv} = 0$ when $u \ne v$ are not adjacent.

results.title: Reduced Laplacian
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a simple graph $G$ on a finite vertex set $V$ and a vertex $r \in V$, the reduced Laplacian of $G$ at $r$ is the integer Laplacian of $G$ with the row and the column of $r$ deleted, a matrix indexed by the vertices of $G$ other than $r$.

results.title: Spanning tree
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A subgraph $T$ of a simple graph $G$ is a spanning tree of $G$ if it contains every vertex of $G$ and, regarded as a graph on its own vertex set, it is a tree (connected and acyclic).

results.title: Number of spanning trees
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a simple graph $G$ on a finite vertex set, the number of spanning trees of $G$ is the number of subgraphs of $G$ that are spanning trees, that is, subgraphs that contain every vertex of $G$ and are trees.

results.title: The integer Laplacian is degree minus adjacency
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a simple graph $G$ on a finite vertex set, the integer Laplacian of $G$ equals $D - A$, where $D$ is the diagonal matrix of vertex degrees and $A$ is the adjacency matrix of $G$, both with integer entries.

results.title: The reduced Laplacian is a principal submatrix
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set $V$ and let $L = D - A$ be its Laplacian matrix over $\mathbb{Z}$, where $D$ is the diagonal matrix of vertex degrees and $A$ is the adjacency matrix of $G$. For every vertex $r \in V$, the reduced Laplacian of $G$ at $r$ equals the submatrix of $L$ obtained by deleting the row and the column of $r$.

results.title: Spanning trees as trees contained in the graph
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a simple graph $G$ on a vertex set $V$, there is an equivalence between the spanning trees of $G$ (subgraphs of $G$ that contain every vertex and are trees) and the simple graphs $H$ on $V$ that are trees with $H \le G$, that is, every edge of $H$ is an edge of $G$. It sends a spanning tree to the graph on $V$ with the same edges.

results.title: Spanning trees as trees on the whole vertex set
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a simple graph $G$ on a finite vertex set $V$, the number of spanning trees of $G$ equals the number of simple graphs $H$ on $V$ such that every edge of $H$ is an edge of $G$ and $H$ is a tree.

results.title: Matrix-tree theorem for a chosen root
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set $V$ and let $r \in V$. Then the determinant of the reduced Laplacian of $G$ at $r$, that is, the integer Laplacian of $G$ with the row and the column of $r$ deleted, equals the number of spanning trees of $G$.

results.title: Matrix-tree theorem for principal minors of the Laplacian
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set $V$, let $L = D - A$ be its Laplacian matrix over $\mathbb{Z}$, where $D$ is the diagonal matrix of vertex degrees and $A$ is the adjacency matrix of $G$, and let $r \in V$. Then the determinant of the submatrix of $L$ obtained by deleting the row and the column of $r$ equals the number of spanning trees of $G$.

results.title: Kirchhoff's matrix-tree theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite nonempty vertex set $V$ and let $r \in V$. Then the determinant of the reduced Laplacian of $G$ at $r$, that is, the integer Laplacian of $G$ with the row and the column of $r$ deleted, equals the number of spanning trees of $G$.
